title.en: Pre-eminence, increase, truth and what is to come

summary: The stream continues with the goods of standing and growth: pre-eminence and lordship, spirit and wrath, victory, greatness and extent; truth and faith, wealth and control, play and joy; what is born and what is to be born, what has been and what will be; good roads, prosperity, fitness and understanding. Sāyaṇa reads many of the pairs as present and future — offspring born and to be born, wealth gained and to be gained — and supplies kalpatām, ‘may it be ready’, to each.

sandhi.rule: final m before a consonant becomes anusvāra (P. 8.3.23), written as the nasal of the following consonant's class (P. 8.4.59): m + c → ñc
final e before a vowel other than a becomes ay (P. 6.1.78) and the y is dropped (P. 8.3.19), leaving the hiatus: me ādhipatyam → ma ādhipatyam

vyakarana.note: Abstract noun (taddhita) from jyeṣṭha ‘eldest, best’: ‘the state of being foremost’ (MW: = jyeṣṭha-tā).

translation.literal: Pre-eminence and for me, lordship and for me, spirit and for me, wrath and for me, force and for me, water and for me [may they be ready].
translation.readable: May pre-eminence be mine, and lordship; may spirit be mine, and wrath, and force; and water.

units.traditional: Sāyaṇa: jyaiṣṭhya is being the most excellent, ādhipatya mastery (स्वामित्वम्). Manyu and bhāma both name kinds of anger: «मन्युभामाशब्दौ क्रोधावान्तरविशेषवाचिनौ»; one is inward (मानसः), the other outward (बाह्यः), shown by signs such as impatience. Ama he takes as immeasurability: «अमोऽप्रमेयत्वं», that opponents cannot take one’s measure. Ambhas is water, cool and sweet: «शैत्यमाधुर्योपेतमुदकम्».

flags.note: corrections.json, C2.1: the second witness (W2) reads भामस् च; classified a W2 error, since visarga before c can only be ś. The text (W1) reads भामश्च.

ama: Monier-Williams gives ‘impetuosity, violence, strength, power’; Sāyaṇa ‘immeasurability’. ambhas: Sāyaṇa ‘water’; MW also gives ‘power, fruitfulness’ (VS, AV), which Keith’s ‘impetuosity’ reflects. The word table gives both senses.
The two witnesses differ on one accent here: W1 marks the svarita on the second syllable of भाम॑श्च, W2 has no mark. The unit is flagged ‘svara under review’; W1’s mark is kept.
Sāyaṇa’s sentence distinguishing manyu and bhāma, «एको मानसोऽक्षमादिलिङ्गजन्यो बाह्यः», seems to have lost a word; it is not said which of the two is the inward and which the outward anger.

sandhi.rule: final ā of the n-stem’s nom. sg. stands before c; so mahimā, varimā, prathimā, varṣmā, drāghuyā
final m before a consonant becomes anusvāra (P. 8.3.23), written as the nasal of the following consonant's class (P. 8.4.59): m + c → ñc

vyakarana.note: jeman, mahiman, variman, prathiman and varṣman are masculine abstracts in -man; the nom. sg. ends in -ā. MW gives jeman ‘victoriousness’ (citing VS 18.4, where the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā has its version of this litany, and TS), variman as the abstract of uru ‘wide’, prathiman of pṛthu ‘broad’.

drāghuyā has the Vedic ending -uyā of adverbs like dhṛṣṇuyā (from dhṛṣṇu), apparently from a u-stem related to dīrgha ‘long’ (compare drāghīyas ‘longer’). The word is not in Monier-Williams; here it stands as an item of the list, ‘length’.
Past participle of √vṛdh used as a neuter noun, beside the action noun vṛddhi.

translation.literal: Victoriousness and for me, greatness and for me, breadth and for me, extent and for me, height and for me, length and for me, what has grown and for me, growth and for me [may they be ready].
translation.readable: May victory be mine, and greatness, breadth and extent, height and length; may increase be mine, and growth.

units.traditional: Sāyaṇa reads these abstracts as the goods of a householder who prevails. Jeman is the capacity to win (जयसामर्थ्यम्); mahiman the wealth that victory brings («महत्त्वं जयसंपादितधनादिसंपत्तिः»); variman being worth choosing and honouring («वरणीयत्वं पूज्यत्वम्»); prathiman the extent of house and fields; varṣman the bodies of sons, grandsons and so on («पुत्रपौत्रादिशरीराणि»); drāghuyā their length, an unbroken line of descent («दीर्घत्वमविच्छिन्ना संततिः»). Vṛddha is abundant food and wealth («प्रभूतमन्नं»), vṛddhi eminence through qualities such as learning.

flags.note: drāghuyā: the stem and case are not certain (no headword in Monier-Williams); the sense ‘length’ follows the root and Sāyaṇa’s दीर्घत्वम्.

variman: Sāyaṇa derives it from ‘choosing’ (वरणीयत्वं); MW gives ‘expanse’ (the abstract of uru), which the sequence with prathiman supports. varṣman: Sāyaṇa ‘the bodies of sons and grandsons’; MW ‘height, top’ and ‘body’.
The printed bhāṣya’s lemma reads गृहिमा where the mantra has महिमा; the gloss (महत्त्वं) shows that महिमा is meant. Its gloss on prathiman also has a misprint (मृह-).

vyakarana.note: jagat, from the reduplicated √gam, ‘moving, living’; as a neuter noun, ‘that which moves or is alive’ (MW). Final t becomes c before ca.
tviṣi, f. i-stem, ‘vehemence; splendour, brilliancy’ (MW); Sāyaṇa takes the second sense.

translation.literal: Truth and for me, faith and for me, the moving world and for me, wealth and for me, control and for me, splendour and for me, play and for me, joy and for me [may they be ready].
translation.readable: May truth be mine, and faith; the living world, and wealth, and mastery; may brightness be mine, and play, and joy.

units.traditional: Sāyaṇa: satya is speaking what is so (यथार्थभाषणम्), and śraddhā «परलोकोऽस्तीति बुद्धिः», the conviction that the other world exists. Jagat is all that moves and does not move. Dhana is gold and the like (सुवर्णादि), vaśa having everything in one’s own control (सर्वस्वाधीनत्वम्), tviṣi the lustre of the body (शरीरकान्तिः). Krīḍā is play such as dice («क्रीडाऽक्षद्यूतादिः»), and moda «तज्जन्यो हर्षः», the gladness born of it.

flags.note: Sāyaṇa’s gloss on jagat is misprinted in the bhāṣya (जगणङ्गमाजङ्गमात्मकम्); its sense, ‘consisting of the moving and the unmoving’, is plain, but it is not quoted.

samasa.meaning: what is well said; a hymn (u + u → ū inside the compound)
what is well done; a good deed, merit

vyakarana.note: Future participle middle (-iṣya- + -māna) of √jan, which is middle in the sense ‘to be born’ (jāyate): ‘about to be born’.
Future participle active of √bhū, n. nom. sg.: ‘what will be’ (MW: n. the future).
Gerundive of √vid ‘to find, acquire’: ‘to be acquired’ (MW 2. vedya, citing TS and VS), paired with the past participle vitta ‘acquired’.

translation.literal: What is born and for me, what is to be born and for me, the well-said and for me, the well-done and for me, what is found and for me, what is to be found and for me, what has been and for me, what will be and for me [may they be ready].
translation.readable: May what is born be mine, and what is yet to be born; the hymn and the good deed; what I have gained and what I am yet to gain; what has been and what will be.

units.traditional: Sāyaṇa reads the pairs as past and future. Jāta is offspring already born (पूर्वसिद्धापत्यम्), janiṣyamāṇa offspring yet to come. Sūkta is «सूक्तमृक्समूहः», a collection of ṛks, and sukṛta «तज्जन्यमपूर्वम्», the unseen merit (apūrva) that comes from it. Vitta is what has been obtained (पूर्वलब्धम्), vedya the wealth still to be gained. Bhūta is fields and the like already secured («पूर्वसिद्धं क्षेत्रादि»), and bhaviṣyat «संपत्स्यमानम्», what will come to be.

sandhi.rule: final m before a consonant becomes anusvāra (P. 8.3.23), written as the nasal of the following consonant's class (P. 8.4.59): m + c → ñc
final e before a vowel other than a becomes ay (P. 6.1.78) and the y is dropped (P. 8.3.19), leaving the hiatus: me ṛddham → ma ṛddham

samasa.meaning: easy to go; an easy way (the vigraha is Sāyaṇa’s gloss)
a good road; pathin takes the compound-final -a (supatha)

vyakarana.note: Past participle of √kḷp ‘to be fit, to be in order’, the root with the vowel ḷ; kḷpti is its action noun. The same root gives kalpatām, the verb Sāyaṇa supplies to every item.
Past participle of √ṛdh ‘to prosper’, beside the action noun ṛddhi; the pattern of vṛddham / vṛddhiḥ in C2.2.

translation.literal: An easy way and for me, a good road and for me, what has prospered and for me, prosperity and for me, what is ready and for me, readiness and for me, understanding and for me, good understanding and for me [may they be ready].
translation.readable: May an easy way be mine, and a good road; what has prospered, and prosperity; what is ready, and the power to make ready; may understanding be mine, and sound judgement.

units.traditional: Sāyaṇa: suga is a place good to go to («सुष्ठु गन्तव्यं»), such as another village where kinsfolk live, and supatha a road free of thieves («चोरादिरहितो मार्गः»). Ṛddha is wealth that has grown or the fruit of rites already performed («धनादिकमनुष्ठितकर्मफलं»), ṛddhi the fruit of a sattra yet to be performed. Kḷpta is a thing fit for its work, kḷpti one’s own capacity (स्वकीयसामर्थ्यम्). Mati is «पदार्थमात्रनिश्चयः», the settled knowledge of ordinary things, and sumati the deciding of hard matters such as the affairs of a kingdom.
